notes: Clicked for credits for about ten straight turns, building up 30+ credits with no plan, and never contested the remote where the Corp advanced and scored three agendas. No coherent plan beyond hoarding credits.
Scored safely behind an iced remote, but slow: many turns spent clicking for credits or drawing while sitting on 10-14 credits. The passive Runner hid the inefficiency.

Ran R&D over and over in the same turn, seeing the same top card again, and drained credits to 0. Sat at 0 credits with a 3-card grip against a Weyland meat-damage deck and was flatlined by Measured Response.
Solid scoring remote behind Hagen and Ansel with good economy and well-timed ADT/Méliès scores. R&D was left behind a single Wave for too long, which let the Runner steal two agendas.

Strong start and eventually won through steady HQ pressure with Docklands Pass. In the midgame it played Tread Lightly into an empty remote, idled on credit clicks, and stayed stuck near 2 credits while ignoring advanced agendas in the remote.
Scored from a lightly iced remote, but left R&D behind one Vertigo all game and lost 6 points there. Spent a whole turn triple-icing a Nico Campaign server instead of protecting R&D.
Good economy setup, got Gauss out with Rigging Up, and kept up remote and HQ pressure for a quick win. Minor oddities: drew with Nuka into a full grip and installed Living Mural on Corp ice.

After a decent early turn it clicked for credits for about 15 turns, reaching 77 credits, never installed a barrier breaker, and almost never ran while the Corp scored repeatedly from one remote. No coherent plan.

Twice played Neurospike for no effect, and heavily iced a remote holding only an Urtica trap. Kept a flood of agendas in HQ behind a single Hafrún without ever adding ice, losing 6 points there, and played double Hedge Fund without spending the money on defense.
Fast-advanced four agendas through a single-ice remote and won despite hovering near 0 credits. R&D stayed open for several turns and economy was thin, but it was an aggressive and workable plan.
Built a 4-ice remote and scored steadily from it. Minor waste: two Oppo Research plays with no tag punishment to follow, and some credit clicks while comfortably rich.

Won with steady single-access HQ runs once Boi-tatá was set up. Kept running into a known, unbreakable Hammer on R&D and lost Maemi, Leech, Cookbook and Fencer, and the economy stayed slow with many credit clicks.

Put an early agenda behind a lone Paywall and lost it, then spent many turns paying 2 credits to trash Stoneship Chart Room and clicking for credits. Held ice in HQ unplayed while at 10-18 credits and left Post-Truth Dividend in HQ to be stolen.

Good early HQ pressure reached 5 points, then it clicked for credits for about ten turns up to 58 credits while the Corp scored unopposed. Late on it ran twice into a known Karunā and took heavy net damage.
Took the Archives steal early and used multi-access and event-driven runs well to win quickly. Minor risk: ran into Jinteki net-damage ice and an Urtica trap with a small grip.

Spent early turns building a 4-ice remote with nothing in it, then could not rez any of it when Ansel placed ADT there, and the agenda was stolen. Later sat on 11-14 credits clicking for credits with agendas and ice stuck in HQ behind a single Tithe.
Early R&D steal was good, but it reran R&D in the same turn for the same card and never built an economy, staying at 0-5 credits. Could not contest the Corp's remote scoring at all.

Left Flower Sermon in a remote behind unrezzed ice with no money to rez, and it was stolen. The economy then collapsed to 0 credits for many turns while it held Hedge Fund and Petty Cash and spent its last credits trashing Runner resources instead of rebuilding.
Strong economy with campaigns, and Ansel kept Server 2 safe for scoring. ADT twice installed agendas into naked new remotes, and Project Ingatan was stolen from one of them.
Clicked for credits nearly every turn up to 88 credits and installed only Unity. It ran just a handful of times, never set up a way into the remote, and the Corp scored out.
